answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a bond for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, and provable fraud burns that bond. Agents serving a lotus nursery, an oasis farm, or a reef survey all face the same rule. Creating more names does not create more bonded capital: an attacker running 1,000 identities must immobilize 1,000 bonds and risks losing each one used to cheat, making a sybil swarm costly rather than free.
